What Genre Is Your Favorite Bass Artist? The Dubstep, Riddim & Melodic Bass Artist Directory

By PLURGASM @plurgasm ⏱ 37 min read

Bass music fans ask the same question every festival season: what genre is this artist, actually? Below is our directory of 96 dubstep, riddim, tearout, melodic bass and adjacent artists. Click any name to see the genres they play, the styles they have played in the past, and who they sound like.

Are you a DJ or producer?

Want to be added, or has your sound changed? Send us your genres and we will update the directory.

Quick Answers: What Genre Is…?

The most searched bass artists, in one line each. Tap a name for the full breakdown.

  • Subtronics Dubstep: riddim and tearout, with newer melodic bass
  • Excision Heavy dubstep, riddim and tearout
  • Skrillex Brostep and dubstep roots, now genre-fluid
  • ILLENIUM Melodic dubstep and future bass
  • Zeds Dead Dubstep, genre-hopping across DnB and hip-hop
  • Seven Lions Melodic dubstep with trance influence
  • SLANDER Melodic bass and heaven trap
  • Svdden Death Riddim and heavy dubstep (VOYD: metal-tinged heavy bass)
  • REZZ Midtempo bass
  • GRiZ Future funk, glitch hop and dubstep
  • Virtual Riot Complex, sound-design-heavy dubstep
  • Ganja White Night Wobble / wonky dubstep
  • Liquid Stranger Experimental wonky bass
  • Sullivan King Metal-meets-dubstep (metalstep)
  • Wooli Heavy and melodic dubstep
  • Kai Wachi Dark heavy dubstep with metal influence

ExcisionHeavy Dubstep · Dubstep · Riddim

What genre is Excision?

Excision is a heavy dubstep artist. He started in drum & bass and early dubstep, became the face of loud, aggressive "brostep"-era bass, and today mostly plays heavy dubstep, riddim and tearout, often with a huge custom production rig.

Heavy DubstepDubstepRiddimDrum & Bass
Who
Jeff Abel
From
Kelowna, BC, Canada
Label
Rottun Recordings, Subsidia (founder)

How the sound changed

  • Roots (2000s) Started as a drum & bass DJ in BC, then moved into early dubstep and founded Rottun Recordings.
  • Shambhala & X Rated (2009–2013) The Shambhala mixes and X Rated (2011) made him the loudest name in North American dubstep.
  • Festival era (2015–now) Albums Codename X, Virus, Apex and Onyx (2022). Founded Lost Lands (2017), Bass Canyon and the Subsidia label. Sets now span riddim, tearout, melodic moments and his slower "Detox" sets.

Start with "Throwin' Elbows" (with Space Laces) · "Gold (Stupid Love)" (with Illenium) · "Bass Head"

Sounds like WooliSullivan KingKai WachiZomboy

ILLENIUMMelodic Dubstep · Future Bass · Dubstep

What genre is ILLENIUM?

ILLENIUM plays melodic dubstep and future bass. His music pairs emotional pop vocals with big dubstep drops, and he is one of the biggest-selling acts melodic bass has produced.

Melodic DubstepFuture BassDubstep
Who
Nick Miller
From
Denver, CO

How the sound changed

  • Ashes era (2016–2018) Ashes and Awake built the emotional, piano-and-vocal future bass sound.
  • Arena era (2019–2023) Ascend, Fallen Embers and the self-titled ILLENIUM (2023) brought rock vocalists and stadium shows.
  • Odyssey (2026) Odyssey (Feb 2026) became another No. 1 dance album and launched a Sphere Las Vegas residency.

Genre Cheat Sheet

Not sure what tearout or wonky means? Here is the short version of every tag used above. Our bass music subgenres guide goes deeper.

  • Dubstep Half-time beats around 140 BPM with heavy, sculpted bass. Started in South London in the early 2000s. More on dubstep →
  • Brostep The loud, mid-range, metal-flavored American take on dubstep from around 2010. Skrillex is the textbook example.
  • Riddim Stripped-back dubstep built on one repeating, bouncy bass pattern. Minimal on purpose. More on riddim →
  • Tearout The most aggressive branch of dubstep: chaotic, distorted, constantly shifting bass and fast fills.
  • Heavy dubstep A catch-all for the harder side of dubstep, from riddim to tearout. Think Lost Lands main stage.
  • Melodic dubstep / melodic bass Emotional chords and vocals with dubstep drops. More on melodic dubstep →
  • Future bass Bright, swelling synth chords and pitched vocals. Softer than dubstep. More on future bass →
  • Midtempo Dark, slow (around 90 to 110 BPM), hypnotic bass. REZZ is the face of it. More on midtempo →
  • Wonky / experimental Groovy, warped, psychedelic bass that skips the usual drop structure.
  • Bass house House tempo (around 125 BPM) with dubstep-style bass. More on bass house →
  • Drum & bass Fast breakbeats around 174 BPM with heavy basslines. More on drum & bass →

FAQ

What is the difference between riddim and tearout?

Riddim repeats one simple bass pattern and leaves space. Tearout does the opposite: it changes sounds constantly and stays aggressive the whole time. Many artists, like Subtronics and Marauda, play both.

Is melodic dubstep the same as future bass?

No, but they overlap. Melodic dubstep keeps a dubstep drop under emotional chords. Future bass swaps the drop for bright, swelling synths. ILLENIUM and Said The Sky move between both.

Is Skrillex still dubstep?

Partly. Skrillex made brostep famous, then spent years in trap, pop, UK garage and house. His 2025 surprise album brought dubstep back to the front of his sets, so the honest answer is dubstep roots, genre-fluid today.

Who is the biggest dubstep artist right now?

By festival draw, Excision, Subtronics and ILLENIUM sit at the top of North American bass, with Skrillex as the crossover giant. Excision also runs two of the biggest bass festivals, Lost Lands and Bass Canyon.

Why do artists have so many genres listed?

Bass artists rarely stay in one lane. Their DJ sets mix styles, and their sound shifts across albums. We list the main genre first, then the others they play or have played.
